provenance.notes: Mid-size rfq kit for asset fleets and warehouse operators with several terminals. Leaned on driver recruiting, lane rate requests and shipper visibility, kept clear of the hotshot kit's single-truck angles. Least sure about the shipper portal and warehouse inventory portal ranges, which depend on their dispatch and warehouse systems.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Company driver and owner-operator lease-on openings by division, home time, pay structure placeholders, equipment assigned, orientation steps and a short mobile application
pageStructurePlus.why: Seated trucks are the whole business. Drivers compare carriers on home time, pay and equipment, from a phone, before they ever call a recruiter.

pageStructurePlus.contains: A page per terminal or yard, regular lanes and regions served, dedicated and one-way service areas, and a coverage map
pageStructurePlus.why: Shippers look for a carrier already running their lanes. Visible lanes and terminals turn a cold search into a rate request.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Dry van, refrigerated, flatbed, dedicated fleets, drayage, consolidation and cross-dock, each with what it suits and how to request capacity
pageStructurePlus.why: Logistics managers buy by mode and equipment first. Each mode needs its own page to be found.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Warehouse locations, space and temperature zones as supplied, pick-pack and kitting, inventory visibility for clients and how the warehouse connects to clients' order systems
pageStructurePlus.why: Shippers moving to outside warehousing compare services and visibility, not square footage alone.

pageStructurePlus.section: Shipper onboarding and lane rate requests
pageStructurePlus.contains: Lane rate request with origin, destination, frequency, equipment and commodity, credit application, insurance certificate request and the onboarding steps
pageStructurePlus.why: A shipper adding a carrier needs rates and paperwork fast. A clear request and onboarding path wins the first load.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Safety programme summary, driver training, maintenance schedule and shop, [safety rating, as supplied] and insurance limits as placeholders
pageStructurePlus.why: Shippers and their insurers check a fleet's safety before awarding freight. Showing the programme plainly answers the question early.

designDirections.name: Drivers Wanted
designDirections.bestFor: Fleets whose most urgent need is seated trucks and a driver application that works from a phone
designDirections.headlineSample: Driving jobs out of {City}, home time you can plan
designDirections.whyItFits: Ultramarine Poster was built for campaigns. Big geometric type and one strong colour make a driver recruiting page read like a billboard.

designDirections.name: Lane Board
designDirections.bestFor: Mid-size asset carriers selling lanes, modes and capacity to shippers and logistics managers
designDirections.headlineSample: Truckload and dedicated freight from {City} terminals
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, and its library entry was made for logistics and fleet operations. Mono labels suit lanes, equipment and terminal data.

designDirections.name: Network Control
designDirections.bestFor: Warehouse and logistics providers selling visibility, integrations and dedicated programmes to larger shippers
designDirections.headlineSample: Warehousing and freight from {City}, visible end to end
designDirections.whyItFits: Deep Space Cyan was made for network dashboards. The dark page and cyan signals present the logistics firm as a control room, not a truck lot.

openers.angle: Driver ads everywhere, thin careers page
openers.line: Your driver openings are posted on every job board, but your own careers page is a paragraph and a phone number. Drivers weighing two carriers look for home time and equipment before they apply.
openers.hook: Find their driver ads on job boards or social profiles, then open the site's careers page and note what's missing.
openers.linkLine: A driver recruiting hub for the fleet: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site mentions owner-operators are welcome but says nothing about settlement, fuel programmes or how lease-on works. Owner-operators pick a trucking company by those details.
openers.hook: Search the site for owner-operator or lease. Note whether pay structure, fuel or settlement are explained.
openers.linkLine: An owner-operator page that answers the lease-on questions: {demo-link}

openers.line: A logistics manager with a weekly lane can only send your fleet a general contact message. A rate request asking origin, destination, frequency and equipment gets you a real freight quote to price.
openers.hook: Look for a quote or rate request form. If it's a generic contact form, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A lane rate request built for shippers: {demo-link}

openers.line: You run trucks out of several terminals, but the site shows one address. A shipper near your other yard has no idea you already run freight from their side of the region.
openers.hook: Count yards and terminals on their maps listings and compare with the site.
openers.linkLine: A page for each terminal with its lanes: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing says warehousing and distribution, but the site is all trucks. A shipper looking for outside warehouse space and pick-pack would never guess you offer it.
openers.hook: Compare their listing categories and posts about the warehouse with what the site's menu shows.
openers.linkLine: Warehouse and fulfilment on its own page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts show refrigerated trailers, but the site never mentions temperature-controlled freight. Food and pharma shippers search for reefer carriers specifically.
openers.hook: Check social posts or yard photos for reefer units or flatbeds, then check whether the site has a page per equipment type.
openers.linkLine: A page for each equipment type the fleet runs: {demo-link}

openers.line: I tried your driver application on my phone and it opened a long form meant for a desktop. Most drivers apply from the cab during a break.
openers.hook: Open the driver application on your phone and note where it breaks or how long it runs. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A driver application that takes five minutes on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no customer login or tracking page on your site. Shippers running freight with several carriers expect to check status without calling dispatch.
openers.hook: Look for a customer login, tracking lookup or document download. If there's none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A shipper tracking and documents page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing on your site describes the fleet's safety programme or driver training. Shippers awarding a dedicated freight account ask for it before rates.
openers.hook: Search the site for safety or training. Never state their rating; only note that the programme isn't shown.
openers.linkLine: A safety and fleet maintenance page: {demo-link}

openers.line: A driver wrote publicly that your company actually gets them home on weekends. That sentence recruits better than any ad, and it's nowhere on your trucking careers page.
openers.hook: Read their employer reviews and social comments from drivers. Copy one phrase about home time, equipment or dispatch.
openers.linkLine: Driver comments on the careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Shippers hunt for overflow warehouse space and extra trucks before the retail peak. The logistics firms with an easy space request get those short-term contracts.
openers.hook: Use this a couple of months before the year-end retail peak or the harvest season in their region.
openers.linkLine: A peak-season warehouse and freight request page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Congratulations on the new tractors you posted about. New equipment is a selling point for drivers and shippers, and your fleet site doesn't mention it.
openers.hook: Find a new trucks, new terminal or expansion post and check whether the site reflects it.
openers.linkLine: The new equipment on the recruiting and capacity pages: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your freight forwarding page lists sea, air and road, but an importer can't send cargo details, incoterms or a target date. The forwarder that asks the right questions gets the booking.
openers.hook: Use for forwarders. Look for a shipment enquiry form with cargo, route and terms fields.
openers.linkLine: A forwarding enquiry that asks for cargo and route details: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Dated site for a modern fleet
openers.line: Your trucks look newer than your website. The layout and footer suggest it hasn't been touched in years, and shippers notice when a carrier's site looks abandoned.
openers.hook: Check the footer year, the layout on a phone and whether recent equipment or lanes appear anywhere.
openers.linkLine: A current logistics site for the same fleet: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is the kind of freight a logistics manager wants proof you can handle. It belongs on a case page for that mode.
openers.hook: Pick their newest haul, project or warehouse post and name it: freight type, equipment and lane.
openers.linkLine: That haul on a freight case page: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — saw the {specific recent job} post, a solid haul.

I went through the {Business Name} site and couldn't find a lane rate request for shippers, or a driver application that works on a phone. I put together a sample with both, plus terminal pages and a warehouse section, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it help if I sent it to you and whoever runs recruiting?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my note got lost between loads. Here's the sample for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a driver recruiting hub with a short phone application, a lane rate request, a page per terminal and equipment type, and a warehouse section. If it isn't useful, tell me and I'll stop.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build recruiting sites and shipper tools for trucking and logistics companies around {City}. I sent you a note a couple of days ago, did it reach you?"

IF NO:
"No problem. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with a driver application that works from a phone, a lane rate request and terminal pages, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Should it go to you, your recruiting manager or sales?"

IF YES:
"What did you and the team think?"
 → let them talk, note whether recruiting or sales is the bigger worry
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting, changes and new openings. For a fleet your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, less than a few weeks of one empty truck."
"Could we take thirty minutes with you and your recruiting lead this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a scope and a deposit invoice. We start with the driver hub so trucks get seated first."

objections.objection: We get drivers from job boards already.
objections.handler: "Keep them. Every driver who sees an ad checks your own site before applying. A careers hub with home time, pay structure and a short phone application turns more of those clicks into applications."

objections.objection: Shippers come through brokers and our sales team.
objections.handler: "Then the site backs up your sales team. Lanes, equipment and a safety page give a logistics manager what they ask your rep for, before the first call."

objections.objection: We have a TMS vendor that does tracking.
objections.handler: "Good. The site links to it or shows its data on your own page under your name. I don't replace the dispatch system; I give shippers a front door."
"You choose. Many fleets show the pay structure, how miles or loads are paid and home time, and give numbers on the call."
"That's when shippers switch carriers on service, and the fleets with lanes and safety visible get the call. It's also the cheapest time to hire good drivers."

"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's a driver hub with a phone application, a lane rate request, terminal and equipment pages and a warehouse section. One seated truck pays it back."

email.subject: Driver hub and lane requests for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build recruiting and shipper sites for trucking companies in {City}, and I made a sample for {Business Name} with a driver application that works on a phone. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} fleet demo down on Friday.

If you or your recruiting lead want it up longer, one word is enough.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — shippers around {City} start lining up peak-season capacity and warehouse space about now. Thought of you.

The trucking site with the driver hub and lane rate request is still here, same price. {demo-link} if you'd like another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a few weeks of an empty truck, which every fleet owner can picture.
Quote the driver hub and phone application first; recruiting pain closes faster than sales pain.
Price each terminal page separately when terminals run their own lanes, recruiters or warehouse.
Anything reading from dispatch or warehouse systems is a separate software project with its own scope.
Expect the owner, the recruiting manager and sales or operations to sign off.
Never publish pay, safety ratings, insurance limits or capacity the company hasn't supplied in writing.

lineItems.item: Driver recruiting hub with mobile application
lineItems.description: Max with company and owner-operator tracks, divisions, home time by route type, a short pre-qualification and recruiter alerts.

lineItems.item: Lane rate request and shipper onboarding
lineItems.description: Max with lane, frequency and equipment fields, spreadsheet upload for lane lists, credit application and routing to sales.
Max with lanes from that terminal, local recruiter, yard photos placeholders and its own openings feed.
Max with equipment specs as supplied, commodities handled, a mode-specific rate request and a cleared case example.
Max with several sites, temperature zones, services by client type and a space request form.
Max with cargo, route, terms, document needs and routing to the right desk by mode.

lineItems.item: Recruiting video set for the careers hub
lineItems.description: Max with several drivers interviewed, a ride-along, terminal walkthroughs and versions cut for social.

whatElseYouSell.name: Driver recruiting ad management
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Driver ads on social and search that send applicants to the trucking careers hub instead of a job board, with cost per application reported each month."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 1, as soon as the recruiting hub is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Fleet and terminal photo and video days
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A day at the terminal shooting clean tractors, the shop and drivers who agree to be filmed gives the recruiting and freight pages real faces."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or when new equipment arrives.

whatElseYouSell.name: Shipper outreach by lane and industry
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each month, a short note to logistics managers at shippers along the fleet's busiest lanes, with a case page and the rate request link."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once lanes and equipment pages are live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profiles for each terminal
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each terminal's profile kept current with hiring posts and freight services, so 'trucking jobs near me' finds the right yard."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, after terminal pages go live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Driver referral programme campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A referral page, cab cards and a text drivers can forward, so the fleet's own drivers bring in the next hires and the bonus is tracked."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once the application is working.

whatElseYouSell.name: Trailer and tractor graphics coordination
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Trailers are rolling billboards on every lane. Matching graphics with the careers address recruit drivers at every truck stop."
whatElseYouSell.when: When they add trailers or rebrand the fleet.

whatElseYouSell.name: Freight case studies by mode
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Plain write-ups of a dedicated freight programme or a warehouse launch, with the shipper named only if they agree."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 4, after sales names two or three good stories.

whatElseYouSell.name: Logistics expo booth and capability sheet
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A booth panel and capability sheet for the regional logistics expo that match the trucking site and send visitors to the rate request."
whatElseYouSell.when: Two months before the logistics show they attend.

withoutAI.route: Truck driving schools they hire from
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The driving school that sends your fleet new drivers needs an enrolment site that shows where graduates get hired. Your recruiter's introduction opens it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Schools sell on placement, and a carrier that hires their graduates is their best reference.

withoutAI.route: Truck repair and tyre shops they use
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The heavy truck shop that handles your overflow repairs sells to every fleet nearby with no booking page. Your maintenance manager's word gets me in."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Repair shops depend on fleet accounts and listen to them.

withoutAI.route: Customs brokers they hand freight to
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The customs broker clearing your cross-border freight needs a document upload and quote page for importers. A carrier partner's referral counts."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Brokers and carriers share shippers and trade referrals.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your leased owner-operators run small trucking businesses with no site. A simple page and invoicing set-up for each, offered through you, keeps them loyal."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Owner-operators trust the carrier they're leased to, and a perk helps retention.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The dealer you bought the new tractors from lists inventory nobody can filter. A fleet customer's introduction gets me to their marketing manager."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Dealers value fleet accounts and need inventory sites with real filters.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The brokerage that tenders you loads needs a carrier sign-up and shipper quote site. Your dispatch manager's referral starts the conversation."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Brokers live on carrier capacity and keep good carriers happy.

withAI.route: Enrolment question assistant for the driving school
withAI.pitchLine: "Would-be truck drivers ask about course length, funding and hiring carriers, and the assistant answers from the school's own information."
withAI.whyItWorks: Schools miss enquiries after hours, and better students reach the carrier.

withAI.route: Repair write-up assistant for the truck shop
withAI.pitchLine: "The technician's notes on a tractor repair become a clear write-up and estimate for the fleet manager to approve."
withAI.whyItWorks: Fleets approve faster, and trucks get back on the road sooner.

withAI.route: Customs document checker for the broker
withAI.pitchLine: "It reads the commercial invoice and packing list and flags missing details before the freight reaches the border, for the broker to confirm."
withAI.whyItWorks: Fewer held loads for the carrier, fewer corrections for the broker.

withAI.whoPays: The carrier, as a perk for leased owner-operators
withAI.pitchLine: "Owner-operators ask why a trucking settlement came out the way it did and get a plain answer from their own statement."
withAI.whyItWorks: Settlement confusion is a top reason owner-operators leave a carrier.

withAI.route: Inventory listing writer for the trailer dealer
withAI.pitchLine: "The dealer uploads a used trucking trailer's spec sheet and the assistant drafts the listing with axle, door and deck details for review."
withAI.whyItWorks: Dealers list a lot of units and hate writing listings.

withAI.route: Load posting writer for the broker
withAI.pitchLine: "Shipper emails become clean load postings with lane, equipment, weight and appointment times for the broker's carriers."
withAI.whyItWorks: Brokers post many loads a day, and cleaner postings get trucks faster.

softwareAI.name: Driver application alerts to recruiters
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every driver application gets an instant text back, and the right terminal's recruiter is alerted within the minute, before the driver applies to another fleet."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30, once the recruiting hub is live. Needs recruiters by terminal and their phones.

softwareAI.name: Driver pre-qualification application
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A short phone application that asks experience, licence class, endorsements and preferred routes first, then collects the full trucking application from qualified drivers."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs hiring criteria by division and the full application they use now.

softwareAI.name: Driver applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It chats with truck driver applicants at night, answers home time and pay structure questions from the fleet's own policy, and books the recruiter call."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, with the pre-qualification. Needs recruiting policies and approved answers. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Shipment status emails at pickup and delivery
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Shippers get a note when freight is picked up, delayed or delivered, drawn from dispatch, so customer service stops fielding status calls."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs status events from the dispatch system and shipper contacts.

softwareAI.name: Lane quote log and win-rate dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every lane rate request and quote in one place, with which lanes the trucking sales team wins and where rates lose."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the rate request form live and recent quotes from sales.

softwareAI.name: Load tender email reader
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tenders that arrive by email are read for pickup, drop, appointment, weight and freight rate, and staged in dispatch for a planner to accept."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a few hundred past tenders and the dispatch entry steps. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Shipper portal for tracking and documents
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Shippers log in to see their freight's status, proof of delivery and invoices, under the logistics company's own name."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs read access to dispatch and billing data and an IT or operations contact.

softwareAI.name: Proof of delivery and invoice sender
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a driver's delivery paperwork is scanned, the invoice and proof of delivery go to the shipper the same day, so freight bills get paid sooner."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs where delivery documents land and the billing export.

softwareAI.name: Dock appointment scheduler
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Carriers and clients book warehouse dock slots online, and the warehouse sees inbound trucks by door and hour."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs dock doors, hours and receiving rules for each warehouse.

softwareAI.name: Driver policy question assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Drivers on the road ask about detention pay, breakdown steps or home time requests and get the fleet's own policy, any hour."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the driver handbook and dispatch rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Warehouse inventory visibility portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Warehouse clients see stock on hand, inbound receipts and outbound orders at the logistics provider without emailing customer service."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs read access to the warehouse system and a client willing to pilot.

softwareAI.name: Driver onboarding portal
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New truck drivers sign forms, upload documents and watch orientation videos before day one, so orientation at the terminal is shorter."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs orientation materials, forms and who checks them.

softwareAI.name: Where-is-my-freight assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Shippers ask by email or chat where a load is and get the dispatch answer with the latest check call, and only exceptions reach customer service."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after status emails. Needs dispatch status data. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Delay explanation drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a freight delivery runs late, it drafts the shipper notice with cause, new time and next steps from the driver's notes, for dispatch to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs past delay messages and dispatch notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Driver document expiry reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Licences, medical cards and permits get reminders before they lapse, sent to the driver and the safety office, so no truck sits for paperwork."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the driver list with each document and its expiry date.

softwareAI.name: Detention and accessorial tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Detention, lumper and layover charges logged with times and proof per load, so the fleet bills every one and shippers can see why."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs arrival and departure times from dispatch and the accessorial rate sheet.

softwareAI.name: Shipper lane bid analyser
softwareAI.pitchLine: "During bid season it reads a shipper's lane spreadsheet and marks which lanes fit the fleet's network and backhauls, for pricing to review."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7, ahead of the shippers' bid season. Needs lane history and current network. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Service scorecards for shippers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each shipper gets a monthly on-time and claims scorecard from the carrier's own data, ready for their quarterly review."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9. Needs delivery times and claims data per shipper.

softwareAI.name: Freight claim file drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Damage photos, delivery notes and the bill of lading become a draft claim response for the trucking claims desk to check."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs past claims and responses. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Safety meeting and incident report drafter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A driver's account and the safety manager's notes become a draft incident report and a fleet safety meeting topic for review."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7. Needs incident forms and past safety meeting topics. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the driver application and screener for carriers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a phone driver application and screener for one fleet. Every mid-size carrier is fighting for the same drivers with a desktop form."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first fleet paid for the build; recruiting pain is the same across carriers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer member carriers a driver recruiting hub template and shipper rate request as a benefit of membership."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons, and one agreement reaches many fleets.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "One page where graduates see which local carriers are hiring new truck drivers, fed from the carriers' own careers hubs."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Schools are judged on placement, and carriers want new drivers early.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The truck dealer or leasing company
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer your fleet customers a recruiting site as part of a lease or purchase, built from the template that already seats trucks."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Dealers sell more tractors to fleets that can seat them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The holding group, per acquired carrier
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "As you buy regional carriers, each gets a recruiting hub and lane pages on one frame, keeping its local name drivers know."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Roll-ups keep local brands to keep drivers, and each acquisition is a repeat build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency signs trucking clients and builds recruiting pages from scratch. License the driver hub and phone application frame."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the relationship; the application flow is what they can't build well.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Same fleet kit in the next freight market
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New carrier clients in a new region
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one mid-size fleet per freight market. {City}'s seat is filled; the next market's best carrier is still open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the build, the pitch and the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every carrier you use uploads insurance and safety documents once, gets tenders and sends delivery proof through one portal."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: You built the carrier side already; the shipper sees the other side of the same paperwork.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Logistics park and free zone tenant directory
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The park owner or free zone authority
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A directory of every warehouse, carrier and forwarder in the park, so shippers see the logistics supply chain in one place."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Parks lease space on the strength of their logistics tenants.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your carrier clients ask for shipper portals that read from the dispatch system you install. I build the customer-facing side."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Resellers get asked for portals they don't build, and the trucking client is proof you can.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Fleet insurance agencies' client safety pages
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer your trucking clients a safety programme page and driver document tracking that make them easier to insure."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies keep fleet clients by helping them look safer to underwriters.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The fleet with a half-built portal
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Half-built shipper portals and dispatch integrations are common in logistics. I finish them, because I've already connected one fleet's dispatch data."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded clients already decided to buy and need someone who has done the integration.

upsellLadder.offer: Fleet site build plus care, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: The owner and recruiting manager approve the demo and scope.
upsellLadder.line: "The site and the care plan sit on one contract, so a new terminal, lane or opening is an email to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first applications arrive through the new careers hub.
upsellLadder.line: "Drivers are applying from their phones. An instant text and a recruiter alert keeps them from applying to the next fleet."

upsellLadder.trigger: Recruiters say they spend evenings answering the same driver questions.
upsellLadder.line: "Your recruiters answer the same home time questions every night. The screener answers truck drivers from your policy and books the call."

upsellLadder.offer: Shipment status emails at pickup and delivery
upsellLadder.trigger: Rate requests turn into new shippers who call dispatch for status.
upsellLadder.line: "Your new shippers are calling for status. Pickup and delivery notes from dispatch end most of those calls."

upsellLadder.offer: Shipper portal for tracking and documents
upsellLadder.trigger: A large shipper asks for a login to see loads and paperwork.
upsellLadder.line: "That shipper wants a login. A portal under your name shows freight, proof of delivery and invoices in one place."

upsellLadder.trigger: The warehouse mentions trucks stacking up at the gate.
upsellLadder.line: "Trucks waiting at the warehouse gate is a scheduling problem. Online dock slots spread them across the day."

upsellLadder.trigger: Shippers' bid season is two months away and sales dreads the lane spreadsheets.
upsellLadder.line: "Bid season is coming. The analyser marks which freight lanes fit your network before pricing starts."

upsellLadder.trigger: A warehouse client asks for live stock visibility, or a prospect asks if you have it.
upsellLadder.line: "Warehouse clients want to see their stock without emailing. A visibility portal is what larger shippers expect from a logistics provider."
